item.subject: maths
item.stem:
The diagram shows quadrilateral $PQRS$ with diagonals $PR$ and $QS$ meeting at $O$. Diya already knows $PR=QS$ and that the diagonals bisect each other, as in a rectangle. She asks what extra diagonal condition makes $PQRS$ a square.

Which two claims are correct?

options.A: The diagonals must also meet at right angles at $O$, so $PQRS$ is a square.
options.B: Call the extra condition the word diagonal and treat that label alone as the square test.
options.C: Equal diagonals that bisect each other and meet at right angles classify $PQRS$ as a square.
options.D: A kite test with one symmetry diagonal alone turns the rectangle construction into a square.
